title: PSI-22 ACME E-FIELD - Electric Field Effects on Flames

title: PSI-25 BASS-II - Burning and Suppression of Solids II
text: 129 solid-fuel tests: PMMA rods, films, slabs and spheres, SIBAL fabric, Nomex and a candle, at 13.6-22.2% oxygen in low-speed forced flow. Outcomes are transcribed from the BASS-II Summary Report. BASS-II results contribute to the combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth. Objectives Include: 1) Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity. 2) Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test #1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity. 3) Provide SoFIE PIs with preliminary data to refine Science Requirements. 4) Practical, realistic (thicker) fuels in typical geometries will be examined, including slabs, cylinders, and spherical sections. The primary variables include: Forced flow velocity (speed and direction); Ambient oxygen concentration (via working volume nitrogen vitiation); Sample geometry (rods, spherical section, slabs, films, and fabric sheets) Variables: Oxygen, Airflow, Flow direction, Outcome, Sample shape, Sample thickness, Sample diameter Instruments: Radiometer, O₂ sensor, CO₂ sensor, CO sensor, Still camera, Anemometer (Air display), Combustion products analyzer (CSA-CP), CO₂ monitor (CDM) Materials: Japan Wax, Nomex, PMMA, SIBAL

title: PSI-26 BASS - Burning and Suppression of Solids

title: 51 of the 111 BASS-II tests with a recorded ending went out when the airflow was turned down or off
text: In microgravity there is no buoyancy to feed a flame, so ventilation does it. Turning the flow down starved 51 flames; at the other end, 12 blew off at high flow.

title: Silicone burned on Earth but barely ignited in space
text: SAFFIRE-II silicone samples left about 0 cm burned in microgravity; in normal gravity three of four burned completely or partly. Earth screening can misjudge materials in both directions.

title: No solid here was tested above 22.2% oxygen. A Moon base plans 30%
text: Every solid-fuel test in this dataset sits below the oxygen level planned for a lunar habitat, and none records reduced pressure or lunar gravity.

title: Silicone burns on Earth but barely in space
text: In SAFFIRE-II, all four silicone samples left about 0 cm burned in microgravity. In normal gravity, samples 2-1 and 2-4 burned completely and 2-2 burned 7.6 cm; only the thickest (2-3, 1.03 mm) failed in both.

title: 7 cool flames recorded in CFI-G
text: CFI-G logged 7 cool flames (regimes PCI-A, PCI-B, PCI-C, PCI-D, PCI-E, PCI-F, PCI-G), all in Butane (30%) at 203 kPa and 38.9-39.9% oxygen. A cool flame burns at low temperature and gives off little light.

title: FLEX: flames that keep burning after they disappear
text: FLEX researchers reported that large heptane droplets kept burning as invisible cool flames after visible extinction. The FLEX table records visible extinction only, so this app marks heptane droplets above 2.4 mm as cool-flame territory rather than counting them as observed cool flames.

title: One material burned out while its neighbour never lit
text: SAFFIRE-II sample 2-7: the PMMA portion was completely consumed while the adjacent Nomex was never ignited.

title: Coverage gap
text: This dataset has no combustion data at any gravity between 0 g and 1 g. Partial-gravity flame tests exist from parabolic flights and LUCI, but not in PSI.

title: Coverage gap
text: No solid fuel in this dataset was tested above 22.2% oxygen, while a lunar habitat is planned at about 30%. Later Saffire flights (IV-VI) studied other atmospheres; their tables are not included here.

title: Coverage gap
text: No solid-fuel table in this dataset records chamber pressure, so no reduced-pressure solid test is recorded.

title: Coverage gap
text: All SAME-R smoke data comes from heated, non-flaming samples: there are no measurements of smoke from genuine flaming fires.

title: Coverage gap
text: No tests here cover electronics, wiring insulation, foams or packaging.

title: Coverage gap
text: BASS (PSI-26) records which samples were burned, but not the conditions or how they ended.

title: Coverage gap
text: SAFFIRE-III records its two burns' conditions but no burn length, spread rate or burn time.
